To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The enzymatic hydrolysis of paper to sugar and fermentation to ethanol and carbon-dioxide by immobilized yeast are an efficient means to convert paper to ethanol and to treat the waste and help preserve the environment; (2) A simultaneous saccharification of newsprint to glucose and ethanol by immobilized yeast was less effective; and (3) A simultaneous hydrolysis and ethanol fermentation was not effective.

the enzymic saccharification of newsprint to glucose and fermentation of glucose to alcohol by immobilization yeast is an efficient and economical process for the conversion of paper waste to ethanol.
In summary, our research is concerned with

two bioprocessing schemes, namely, enzymic hydroly-sis of newsprint to glucose and its subsequent conversion to ethanol and carbon-dioxide by immobilized yeast cells and a simultaneous sacchari-fication and fermentation of paper slurry by cellulase and yeast cells.
the development of a bioprocess for conversion of solid-wastes (newsprint) to clean fuel (ethanols) using enzymes (cellulase and cellobiose) and yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae).

the conversion of solid-wastes (newsprint) to an environmentally safe clean fuel (ethanal) by enzymic saccharification of cellulose to glucose and fermentation of glucose to ethanal by immobilized yeast.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

enzymic hydrolyzation of newsprint to glucose followed by fermentation of glucose to alcohol is a viable and efficient method for the conversion of newsprint to ethanol, a clean fuel, and carbon dioxide, a harmless gas.
the process of saccharification and subsequent fermentation of newsprint waste is feasible and is an efficient means to produce a clean fuel (ethyl alcohol).
the enzymic saccharification and yeast fermentation is an efficient and feasible process for conversion of paper slurry into ethanol and CO2.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed two bioprocess systems for conversion of paper waste to an environmentally clean fuel (ethyl alcohol).
the enzymic saccharification of the newsprint to glucose and the fermentation of glucose to alcohol by immobilization of yeast is a feasible process to produce a clean fuel from solid-waste.
enzymic hydrolyses of newsprint waste is a feasible process to convert the waste to an environmentally acceptable clean fuel (ethyl alcohol).
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of cellulase and cellosiobase to hydrolyze newsprint to sugar followed by the fermentation of the sugars to alcohol and carbon dioxide is an efficient means to treat the solid-waste and to produce a clean fuel.
enzymic hydrolyzation and fermentation of newsprint to ethanol is a viable alternative to burning newsprint in an incinerator.
the enzymic saccharification and subsequent fermentation of newsprint waste into ethanol is a viable and environmentally safe alternative to the conventional energy production from solid-waste.
